dataNotes.title: Costs tab total double-counts TART Main Line
dataNotes.text: The costs tab total ($23.08 million, K25) sums the Main Line subtotal (row 16) and its three segments (rows 13–15), counting about $2.50 million twice. This model counts the segments once.
dataNotes.cite: Example Transit Financial Scenario Workbook.xlsx › costs K25, K13:K16

dataNotes.title: Route 30 cost rate
dataNotes.text: The costs tab prices Route 30 at the Lake Link Via rate ($68.70/VSH, $240,450). The model now uses $147.80/VSH (about $517,300) per TRPA (Oct. 23, 2026), matching VRH Rates and the FY 26-27 Emerald Bay Shuttle budget of $517,288.
dataNotes.cite: Example Transit Financial Scenario Workbook.xlsx › costs J7; VRH Rates J10; Financial PlanG.xlsx › T2-4 G20

dataNotes.title: VSH shares that sum to less than 100 percent
dataNotes.text: On Financial PlanG, TART total VSH (Operating Stats F45) includes Main Line and its segments, so TART 5307 shares on Revenue %s sum to 72 percent. LCTOP and interest shares divide by TTD hours including Route 30 but give Route 30 nothing (90 percent). The model uses the corrected bases from Funding Model V1G.
dataNotes.cite: Financial PlanG.xlsx › Operating Stats F43, F45; Revenue %s rows 3, 15, 20; Funding Model V1G.xlsx › Operating Stats F45, F48

dataNotes.title: TDVA formula error
dataNotes.text: Per Route Model row 28 multiplies the Nevada State Parks amount (D27, $85,000) instead of the TDVA amount (D28, $120,000). The model uses $120,000.
dataNotes.cite: Financial PlanG.xlsx › Per Route Model O28

dataNotes.title: TDA labels on the per-route model
dataNotes.text: Per Route Model D19 and D21 are labeled LTF and STA but hold TTD's rural one-third and urban two-thirds of LTF plus STA ($615,042 and $1,230,085), and no route formulas use them. The model uses LTF $1,263,326 and STA $581,801 from Table A1 with the TDA shares on Revenue %s.
dataNotes.cite: Financial PlanG.xlsx › Per Route Model D19, D21; T2-4 G66:G67

dataNotes.title: TART FTA 5307 amount
dataNotes.text: The per-route model uses $1,653,136 (75 percent of Placer's earned share). TART's financial plan (Table A2) budgets $2,660,000, including 5307 directed through PCTPA. The model uses TART's number per TRPA (Oct. 23, 2026).
dataNotes.cite: Financial PlanG.xlsx › Per Route Model E12; T5-7 G59

dataNotes.title: TNT/TMA service costs
dataNotes.text: The costs tab estimates NLTE at $241,181 (1,200 VSH) and Park & Ride at $602,952 (3,000 VSH) at $200.98/VSH. The TNT/TMA FY 26-27 budget shows NLTE $694,260 and Park & Ride $894,233, which is what its revenues are sized to. TNT/TMA program administration ($321,870) and regional marketing ($223,823), and the membership, management, and marketing revenues that pay for them, are outside the per-route model.
dataNotes.cite: Example Transit Financial Scenario Workbook.xlsx › costs rows 22–24; Financial PlanG.xlsx › TNTTMA $ F22, F43, K22, Q22

dataNotes.title: LCTOP on Nevada routes
dataNotes.text: The State Funds fact sheet restricts LCTOP to California, but the draft shares on Revenue %s assign part of it to Nevada routes 19X, 22, and 28. The model flags these cells.
dataNotes.cite: State Funds – FINAL.pdf › LCTOP; Financial PlanG.xlsx › Revenue %s row 15

dataNotes.title: Federal funds above the operating share
dataNotes.text: At the costs tab route costs, the draft shares put more federal money on Routes 19X, 22, and 50 than the 50 percent operating share allows, and TTD holds more 5311 than its two rural routes can absorb at 50 percent. TTD's own per-route worksheet uses $912,052 of the $1,798,577 in 5311. Confirm how the remainder is used (administration, capital, or other routes).
dataNotes.cite: Financial PlanG.xlsx › T2-4 Q146:R146

dataNotes.title: Fact sheet items not in the FY 26-27 plan
dataNotes.text: Nevada State general fund allocation to TTD ($346,500 in FY 25-26) stays at $0: it was not addressed in the Oct. 23 answers. The local appropriation for TTD planning and administration ($232,235), Martis Zones of Benefit ($50,000), the seven Lake Link private partners ($302,100), and the North Tahoe Community Alliance ($487,173) are now carried at their FY 25-26 amounts per TRPA (Oct. 23, 2026).
dataNotes.cite: State Funds – FINAL.pdf › Nevada State; Local Funds 1 of 2 – FINAL.pdf › Local Appropriation, Martis Zones of Benefit

dataNotes.text: TDVA is $65,000 on the fact sheet (FY 25-26) and $120,000 in the FY 26-27 plan. The Travel North Tahoe Nevada card shows "TTD budgeted $8,000" though the funded system is NLTE. TRPA (Oct. 23, 2026): use the plan amount ($120,000).

dataNotes.title: Electrification credits
dataNotes.text: Revenue %s notes call electrification credits "not real money, only used as match." The fact sheet lists $8,000 budgeted for TTD operations. The model counts them as match only; this can be switched in Details.

dataNotes.title: Match rates for NDOT 5311
dataNotes.text: Revenue %s lists 50 percent non-federal match for 5311; partner notes say NDOT match is 20 percent for administration, 40 percent for operating, and 5 percent for capital. TRPA (Oct. 23, 2026): go with 50 percent non-federal for now; we can change it later.
dataNotes.cite: Financial PlanG.xlsx › Revenue %s C6, F64

dataNotes.title: Lake Link and placeholder jurisdiction shares
dataNotes.text: Jurisdiction shares split each service equally among the jurisdictions in the costs tab, except Lake Link (one-third Douglas, two-thirds CSLT). ADA paratransit services have no local conditions listed. Lake Link VSH are contract hours, not actuals.
dataNotes.cite: Example Transit Financial Scenario Workbook.xlsx › costs columns C, U12

dataNotes.cite: Financial PlanG.xlsx › T2-4 G72:H72

dataNotes.cite: Financial PlanG.xlsx › T2-4 rows 21, 29

dataNotes.title: Vanpools
dataNotes.text: Revenue %s has a Vanpools column, but the costs tab has no vanpool row. The model includes vanpools at the TNT/TMA FY 26-27 budget ($195,800).
dataNotes.cite: Financial PlanG.xlsx › Revenue %s AC1; TNTTMA $ K43

dataNotes.title: Open questions in the source files
dataNotes.text: "What revenues can we count on for 27-28 for Lake Link?" and "Do we recommend Transportation user fee?" A new regional source can be tested with Add source on the Funding sources tab.
dataNotes.cite: Financial PlanG.xlsx › Questions F4, F6

dataNotes.title: Fixed costs for contractors
dataNotes.text: The costs tab notes that fixed costs could be separated out, but that is harder for private contractors, and fixed costs change with large service changes. The model uses fully allocated rates.
dataNotes.cite: Example Transit Financial Scenario Workbook.xlsx › costs W4

dataNotes.title: Funding rule decisions from the funding lead (Oct. 23, 2026)
dataNotes.text: No optimizer: the tool flags problems and shows trade-offs. Match is tested per grant, per recipient. 5307 operating at 50 percent non-federal; 5310 at 20 percent non-federal (to confirm); NDOT 5311 at 50 percent for now. Fares count as local match. Toll credits are assumed unavailable. “Ideally used in” conditions are preferences, and using a source outside its intended jurisdiction is allowed but highlighted. Jurisdiction cost splits stay even-split placeholders for now. Capital is out of scope for this iteration; planning and administration funds are in scope.
dataNotes.cite: TRPA (Oct. 23, 2026)

dataNotes.title: South Tahoe Transit JPA
dataNotes.text: The JPA is not an operator, and the working assumption is that it will not become one (TRPA, Oct. 23, 2026). South shore fixed route funding stays with TTD in this model.
dataNotes.cite: TRPA (Oct. 23, 2026)

dataNotes.title: Funding cliffs with no defined replacement
dataNotes.text: SB 125 ends after FY 26-27 ($1,575,000 across TTD and Lake Link) and the Route 30 pilot funds end after FY 27-28. No replacement funding is defined yet; TRPA (Oct. 23, 2026) asked that this be highlighted as a gap and a need. See the Five-year outlook tab.
dataNotes.cite: TRPA (Oct. 23, 2026)

dataNotes.title: Scenario presets
dataNotes.text: The scenario bar can apply three requested scenarios (TRPA, Oct. 23, 2026): keep TDA and SB 125 in California only, federalize Lake Link, and TTD absorbs Lake Link with its revenue streams. Each preset is a set of logged edits on top of the current scenario; Reset returns to the source data.
dataNotes.cite: TRPA (Oct. 23, 2026)
